Costas Lemos Innovation Programme Scholarship

The Costas Lemos Innovation Programme (CLIP) Scholarships have been established to equip excellent Greek students with the tools to confront our most pressing environmental challenges. Up to five CLIP Scholarships are provided annually to students who have completed undergraduate studies in Greece, and hold either a Greek passport or Greek residence, offering full coverage of tuition fees and a contribution to living expenses for 24 months.

The CLIP Scholarships are administered by the CML Foundation in collaboration with Delft University Fund.
The scholarships are available to students entering the academic year 2026 for one of the following specific TU Delft Master of Science Programmes:

  • MSc Earth, Climate and Technology;
  • MSc Environmental Engineering;
  • MSc Geomatics;
  • MSc Strategic Product Design;
  • MSc Integrated Product Design;
  • MSc Sustainable Energy Technology;
  • MSc Marine Technology.

How to apply

Students can apply for the scholarship after they have received an Admission Letter for one of the above Master’s programmes. Students must apply and submit all of the following documents:

  • Scholarship Application Form;
  • Admission Letter;
  • Undergraduate Degree Transcript with GPA;
  • Curriculum Vitae (CV);
  • One or two references;
  • Motivation Letter (to include anything additional not already included in the Scholarship Application Form).

Application deadline: July 31, 2026
Submit application form and attachments to ufonds@tudelft.nl

Download application form

Selection process

  1. Delft University Fund reviews the applications and proposes the candidates to CML Foundation.
  2. The CML Foundation assesses the financial need and environmental vision of candidates, and decides to whom to provide a scholarship.
  3. An interview with applicants may be part of the process. Our aim is the complete the selection process by 1 September, 2026.
  4. The payment of the scholarship funds to the student will start once the student has begun their Master’s programme at TU Delft.

The scholarship will be paid to the student directly by Delft University Fund when all obligations by the student have been met.
